expected.reference_answer: Data hazards arise from data dependencies. Control hazards arise from branches and other changes in control flow. Structural hazards arise from contention for hardware resources.

Control hazards arise from branches and other changes in control flow.
Structural hazards arise from contention for hardware resources.

evidence.quote:
¡ Any condition that causes the pipeline to

¡
Result: Much bubbles and degraded efficiency

¡
Data Hazard: Stall due to dependencies of some 
data
¡
Read-after-write (RAW)
¡
Write-after-write (WAW)
¡
Write-after-read (WAR)
¡
Control Hazard: Stall due to branch and 
synchronization
¡
Structural hazard: Stall due to contention on 
hardware such as memory channel, cache slot, 
queue, etc.

expected.reference_answer: Threads in the same warp follow different execution paths. Executing with only a subset of active threads reduces SIMD utilization.

rubric.criterion: Threads in the same warp follow different execution paths.
Executing with only a subset of active threads reduces SIMD utilization.

evidence.quote:
GPU: Optimize Throughput of a Large Number of Simple Threads
¡ A GPU uses a SIMD pipeline to save area on 
control logic
¡
Groups scalar threads into warps
¡ Branch Divergence
¡
Occurs when threads inside warps branch to 
different execution path
¡ Result: Only a subset of threads execute, 
waste SIMD pipeline utilization

input.question: Why does adding arbitrarily many processors fail to deliver unlimited speedup for a fixed-size program?
input.instruction: Answer using only the current lecture. Explain your reasoning or show the calculation and cite the physical PDF page numbers. If the material is insufficient, say so explicitly.

expected.reference_answer: For fixed problem size, S(p) = 1 / ((1-f) + f/p). f is the parallelizable fraction. The serial fraction limits maximum speedup.

rubric.criterion: For fixed problem size, S(p) = 1 / ((1-f) + f/p).
f is the parallelizable fraction.
The serial fraction limits maximum speedup.

evidence.quote:
Performance Models
¡ When problem size is fixed, even a small serial fraction caps total speedup
Amdahl's Law: The Serial Fraction Wins
S(p) = 1 / ((1 - f) + f / p)
f: parallelizable fraction
1 - f: serial fraction
p: number of processors / threads
NUMERICAL INTUITION
f = 0.90
max speedup -> 10x
f = 0.99
max speedup -> 100x
FIXED PROBLEM SIZE
serial
parallelizable work
More processors squeeze the blue part, but 
the purple serial part remains.
